summary: console.log() displays text and values in the console. Every console.log() starts a new line.
notes: Text goes in quotes. Single quotes, double quotes, and backticks all make strings.
Commas between values add a space automatically.
Statements usually end with a semicolon. JavaScript can insert missing ones, but writing them avoids surprises.
pitfall: Writing console.Log with a capital L causes TypeError: console.Log is not a function. JavaScript is case-sensitive.
contrast: JavaScript's console.log() works like Python's print(): it ends the line and puts spaces between values. In a browser it writes to the developer tools console, not the page.
